title_src: Trading hustle for balance: the quiet rise of the “slow career”
title_zh: 用“拼命”换“平衡”：慢职业的悄然崛起

theme_words.meaning_zh: 慢职业：主动放缓职业节奏的生活方式
拼命打拼；忙碌奔忙（常含过度之意）
注意到；留意并采取行动

words.note_zh: 常修饰 employer / university / award

words.meaning_zh: 强度极大的，令人吃不消的
words.note_zh: 本义“惩罚性的”，a punishing schedule 即“高强度排班”
career ladder 职业阶梯；climb the ladder 逐步晋升
注意重音 /prəˈməʊʃn/；动词 promote

words.meaning_zh: 慢职业：主动放缓职业节奏
words.note_zh: 全文核心概念，也可作定语：the slow-career movement

structure.text: they are choosing shorter hours, smaller cities and jobs（三个并列宾语）
Rather than chasing promotions —— rather than + doing 表示“而不是……”，置于句首加强对比
that leave room for the rest of life —— 修饰 jobs，其中 leave room for 意为“给……留出空间”

sentences.text: Rather than chasing promotions, they are choosing shorter hours, smaller cities and jobs that leave room for the rest of life.
sentences.tip_zh: 写作迁移：先摆出旧观念（rather than…），再给新选择，对比结构清晰，适合议论文开头段。

paragraphs.text: For decades, the surest route to success was thought to run through the city centre: a prestigious employer, a [[punishing]] schedule and a clear ladder to climb. Yet a growing number of young graduates are quietly stepping off that ladder. Rather than chasing promotions, they are choosing shorter hours, smaller cities and jobs that leave room for the rest of life. Sociologists call it the “[[slow career]]” — and it is spreading fast.
paragraphs.zh: 几十年来，人们认为通往成功最有把握的路线要穿过市中心：进入名企、接受高强度的排班、沿着清晰的阶梯往上爬。然而，越来越多的年轻毕业生正悄悄走下这架梯子。他们不再追逐晋升，而是选择更短的工时、更小的城市，以及能给生活其余部分留出空间的工作。社会学家称之为“慢职业”——而且它正迅速蔓延。

words.note_zh: 生动用法：Rent swallows up most of my income.
本义“微积分”；the calculus of… 即“对……的利害权衡”
不可数名词时常不加冠词
consultant 咨询顾问
trade a fifth of their pay for two extra days off；同义 swap A for B

structure.text: but so does the feeling —— “so + 助动词 + 主语”表示“……也一样”，避免重复 matters
that one’s time is one’s own —— 解释 the feeling 的具体内容

sentences.text: Money still matters, but so does the feeling that one’s time is one’s own.
sentences.tip_zh: “so does / so is + 名词”是考研英语写作高频倒装句式，用来并列强调第二个论点。

paragraphs.text: The trend is partly economic. When housing costs swallow half a salary and promotions arrive slowly, the [[calculus]] of overwork changes. A survey by a Beijing consultancy found that nearly 40% of workers born after 1995 would [[trade A for B|trade a fifth of their pay for]] two extra days off each week. Money still matters, but so does the feeling that one’s time is one’s own.
paragraphs.zh: 这一趋势部分源于经济因素。当房价吞掉一半工资、晋升又姗姗来迟时，人们对“加班是否值得”的盘算就变了。北京一家咨询公司的调查发现，近 40% 的 95 后员工愿意用五分之一的薪水换取每周多两天休息。钱当然重要，但“时间属于自己”的感觉同样重要。

words.note_zh: 反义 tighten；the link between A and B
swap A for B：用 A 换 B，与 trade 用法相近
on the payroll 即“在编、在职”
字面“缝合”；stitch together a living 凑一份生计
make sth viable 使……变得可行；名词 viability

structure.text: Remote work has loosened the link（远程办公弱化了这种关联）
between where people live and where people earn —— 两个 where 从句作 between 的宾语，平行结构
allowing graduates to swap A for B without leaving the payroll —— 现在分词表结果；without + doing 表示“无需……”

sentences.text: Remote work has loosened the link between where people live and where they earn, allowing graduates to swap Shanghai rents for Chengdu comfort without leaving the payroll.
sentences.tip_zh: swap Shanghai rents for Chengdu comfort 是“借代”修辞：用房租代指大城市压力，用地名+comfort 构成对仗，适合写作模仿。

paragraphs.text: Technology has helped. Remote work has [[loosen|loosened]] the link between where people live and where they earn, allowing graduates to swap Shanghai rents for Chengdu comfort without leaving the payroll. Digital platforms also make side projects [[viable]]: a part-time illustrator or online tutor can stitch together a modest living without a single office day.
paragraphs.zh: 技术起到了助推作用。远程办公弱化了“住在哪里”和“在哪里挣钱”之间的绑定，让毕业生们不必离职，就能用上海的房租换来成都的舒适。数字平台也让副业变得可行：一名兼职插画师或线上家教，一天办公室都不用去，也能拼凑出一份体面的生计。

words.note_zh: a luxury (that) … cannot afford 买不起的奢侈品
the ambitious 作名词：“有野心的人群”
re- 前缀：rethink / reshape / rebrand
注意与 refuse 的语体差别，reject 更书面
crowd out everything else 挤掉其他一切；名词形式 crowd-out

structure.text: less about A than about B —— “与其说是 A，不如说是 B”
about laziness / about redefining the good life —— 两个 about 短语保持形式对称

sentences.text: Yet the movement is less about laziness than about redefining the good life.
sentences.tip_zh: “less A than B / not A but B” 是让步反驳段的黄金句式：先承认对方观点，再换角度立论。

paragraphs.text: Critics warn that slow careers are a luxury the ambitious cannot afford — and a trap for women, who still do most of the care work at home. There is truth in this. Yet the movement is less about laziness than about redefining the good life. Young workers are not rejecting work itself; they are rejecting work that [[crowd out|crowds out]] everything else.
paragraphs.zh: 批评者提醒说，慢职业是一种“有野心的人消费不起”的奢侈品——而且对女性是个陷阱，因为家务和照料工作仍大多落在女性身上。这话不无道理。然而，这场运动与其说是懒惰，不如说是对“美好生活”的重新定义。年轻工作者否定的不是工作本身，而是那份会挤占一切其他东西的工作。

words.meaning_zh: 成长轨道（公司内非线性晋升通道）
words.note_zh: 与 fast track（快车道）相对
take a career break 主动暂停工作
housing subsidies 住房补贴；动词 subsidise/subsidize
lighter commutes 更轻松的通勤；commuter 通勤族

words.meaning_zh: 注意到；留意并采取行动
words.note_zh: 比 pay attention to 更书面，常用于新闻语体
也可写 talent war；war on / war for 搭配不同

structure.text: The message is clear（信号很明确）
冒号后整句是对 message 的展开，英文常用冒号引出具体论断
not only with pay, but with time —— not only … but (also) … 并列两个介词短语，with 表“凭借”

sentences.text: The message is clear: the war for talent will be won not only with pay, but with time.
sentences.tip_zh: 结尾金句式：not only with A, but with B 将抽象竞争落到两个具体维度，适合文章收束段模仿。

paragraphs.text: Employers are [[take note|taking note]]. Several large tech firms in China now offer “growth tracks” that pause rather than punish career breaks, while smaller cities compete for talent with housing subsidies and lighter commutes. The message is clear: the [[the war for talent|war for talent]] will be won not only with pay, but with time. The generation that grew up being told to run faster is learning, at last, to choose its own pace.
paragraphs.zh: 雇主们已经注意到了。中国的几家大型科技公司如今提供“成长轨道”，允许职业空窗期暂停而非惩罚；小城市则用住房补贴和更轻松的通勤来争夺人才。信号很明确：人才争夺战的胜负，不只取决于薪水，还取决于时间。这一代从小被要求“跑快点”的人，终于在学习选择自己的节奏。

background.body_zh: “慢职业”并非不工作，而是主动选择非线性的职业路径：降低工时与通勤、接受晋升放缓、把家庭与个人成长放在与工作同等的位置。它与“内卷”（involution）互为镜像，也常与“躺平”（lying flat）被一同讨论，但慢职业强调的是“选择节奏”，而非退出竞争。

background.title_zh: 延伸阅读：四天工作制试验
background.body_zh: 2022 年以来，英国、日本、西班牙等国的多项“四天工作制”试验报告显示：多数参与企业营收与员工满意度双升、离职率下降。本文中“用五分之一薪水换两天休息”的调查数据，正呼应了全球范围内“时间比金钱更稀缺”的价值观迁移。

expressions.zh: 穿过市中心（喻指通往城市中心的路径）
expressions.usage_zh: 引申为“通往……的路线”：the surest route to success runs through…
与 climb the ladder（爬上阶梯）相反，写“反内卷”话题必备
同义：swap A for B；trade a fifth of their pay for two extra days off
leave room for the rest of life 给生活留空间
Work that crowds out everything else 挤占一切其他的事

expressions.expr: not only with A, but with B
expressions.usage_zh: 收束段强调句式，with 表“凭借、用”

quiz.q: According to the article, why are young workers choosing “slow careers”?
options: Because they have lost interest in any kind of work.
Because high living costs and slow promotions change the calculus of overwork.
Because the government requires firms to shorten working hours.
Because remote technology has made offices unnecessary.
quiz.explanation_zh: 第二段明确指出：当房价吞掉一半工资、晋升又慢，人们对加班的权衡（the calculus of overwork）就变了。A 与第四段“not rejecting work itself”矛盾；C 文中未提；D 过度推断，远程办公只是助推因素之一。
punishing 本义“惩罚性的”，形容 schedule 时指“强度大到让人吃不消的”，即 extremely demanding。

quiz.q: What does “the movement is less about laziness than about redefining the good life” imply?
options: Young people are becoming lazier than before.
The good life has been defined by laziness.
It is more a new definition of the good life than laziness.
Laziness is the main reason for slow careers.
quiz.explanation_zh: less about A than about B = “与其说是 A，不如说是 B”，重心在后者：这是对“美好生活”的重新定义。

quiz.q: Young workers are not rejecting work itself; they are rejecting work that ______ (crowd out) everything else.
quiz.explanation_zh: 定语从句先行词是 work（不可数/单数），从句谓语用第三人称单数；且 reject 的宾语是“挤占一切的工作”，与前半句形成 not A but B 的对仗。

writing.title_zh: 写作练习：A letter on work-life balance
writing.prompt_zh: 假定你是李华，校英文报正在讨论“毕业后该追求高薪还是慢节奏”。请写一篇 150 词左右的短评：1）概述两种观点；2）表明你的立场；3）至少使用 2 个本文学到的表达（如 trade A for B / crowd out / not only with A, but with B）。

lead_zh: 几十年来，成功的标准路径似乎只有一条：挤进大城市、进入名企、拼上九九六，然后一级一级往上爬。但越来越多的年轻毕业生正在悄悄走下这架梯子——他们选择更短的工时、更小的城市，以及给生活留出空间的工作。社会学家称之为“慢职业”（slow career）。本文学习除了职场高频词，还能掌握 trade A for B、crowd out、take note 等地道表达，适合四六级与考研写作迁移。
discussion_zh: Would you trade part of your salary for more free time? Why or why not?
“慢职业”在中国常被与“躺平”相提并论。你认为二者有何不同？
What can universities and employers do to make work more sustainable for young people?
